picks.title: Hundreds Sue Meta for Copyright Infringement, Rejecting Class Action Payouts
picks.excerpt: Nearly 300 authors are suing Meta over AI training on pirated books, seeking a jury trial and the maximum $150,000 per infringement rather than class-action payouts; attorney Kyle Roche says many more cases are coming.
picks.rationale: A new filing: nearly 300 authors opt out of class payouts and sue Meta individually for up to $150,000 per infringed work, which gives authors a new way to pursue AI-training claims.

picks.title: Publisher cuts ties with Quebec author accused of AI use in award-winning novel
picks.excerpt: Éditions du Boréal said AI was used in Thélyson Orélien's novel C'était ça ou mourir, contrary to his denials, citing traces of AI tags in document metadata, and ended its relationship with the author.
picks.rationale: Follow-up with a new action: the publisher confirms AI use from document metadata and drops the author. This is the first publisher-confirmed case in the Orélien affair.

picks.title: [단독] 한강·황석영 책 도둑질, 화웨이 등 中 AI기업도 가세했다
picks.excerpt: 앤트로픽에 이어 중국 화웨이도 AI 모델 '판구 시그마' 학습에 한강·황석영 등 한국 작가의 책을 무단으로 내려받은 것으로 기술보고서를 통해 확인됐다.
picks.rationale: A new revelation: Huawei's own technical report shows Korean authors' books in its Pangu training data. It is a different company from the Anthropic case published on 10-16.

picks.title: Society of Authors withdraws from Ethical AI Charter after member backlash
picks.excerpt: The Society of Authors has withdrawn from the Ethical AI Charter it launched last week, following member backlash and a clarifying statement from CEO Anna Ganley on its position on generative AI.
picks.rationale: Follow-up with a new decision: a founding signatory leaves the Ethical AI Charter a week after its launch because members objected.

picks.title: Survey Finds Book Buyers Split on AI Use
picks.excerpt: A BookInsights.ai study finds younger readers more open to authors using AI in some form, but readers of all ages agree that books should disclose AI use.
picks.rationale: New reader data: younger buyers are more open to authors using AI, but readers of all ages want AI use disclosed, which gives disclosure policy a direct reader basis.

https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/.new_action: On 10-21 publisher Éditions du Boréal confirmed AI use (from AI tags in the document metadata) and ended its relationship with the author. Earlier cards covered the 9-24 accusation and the 9-26 removal from the Goncourt list.

https://www.thebookseller.com/news/socie.new_action: The Society of Authors formally withdrew from the Ethical AI Charter, which launched on 10-15, after member backlash.
